reason: This passage (Exodus 1) explicitly contrasts two models of leadership and conduct: Pharaoh commands violence (infanticide) against Hebrew children as a tool of control, while the midwives Shiphrah and Puah refuse this violence and instead fear God. The text rewards the midwives' non-violent obedience to God—they are blessed with established households—while Pharaoh's violent approach proves ineffective (the Hebrew population multiplies despite his brutality). The passage presents fear of God and refusal to commit violence as virtuous, not violence as a model for good leadership.
